legato-systems-inc.note: IPO 1995 (the firm's own listing), acq. by EMC for $1.3B in 2003. Client/server storage management, funded 1988.

linkedin.note: Greylock led the $10M SERIES B announced 2004-10-13, David Sze on the board through the 2011 IPO. acq. by Microsoft for $26.2B in 2016. Golden-set row.

lithos.note: Enhanced rock weathering on farmland for carbon removal; a 2023 seed.

llamaindex.note: The data framework for LLM applications; Greylock seeded it (Jerry Chen).

lookout.note: Mobile security. The consumer business went to F-Secure in 2024 and the enterprise SSE business to Fortinet in 2025, so the 2014 $1B mark no longer stands — the collapse-evidence rule of §6, which cites this company. below_1b.

lumigent.note: Database audit and compliance software funded 2003; the company wound down.

lunar.note: IPO 1990 (the firm's own listing), acq. by GE Medical Systems, 2000. Bone densitometry, funded 1986.

lyra.note: Lyra Health, workforce mental-health care; Greylock announced the investment in Oct 2015 and the site records a seed entry, which for a company the firm backed at formation is the class where that claim holds. Last raised at $5.58B in 2022 — pinned in the A/B pass.

lytro.note: Light-field photography funded 2012 (Don Sullivan is the Greylock person on the firm's own card); the company wound down in 2018 and Google took the patents and much of the team. Acquired with a successor on the wind-down-then-asset-sale reading (§6).

magic-eden.note: NFT and multi-chain marketplace; site states a Series A entry. Raised at $1.6B in 2022 — pinned in the A/B pass.

magical.note: Ambient automation for repetitive work; a 2021 seed.

mainspring-communications-inc.note: Mainspring, internet strategy consulting funded 1996; IPO 2000 and acq. by IBM, 2001.

mainspring-inc.note: The same Mainspring position under its second listed name; IPO 2000 and acq. by IBM, 2001. Merged onto mainspring-communications-inc in identity-merges.json and collapsed at the rebuild.

maker-communications.note: IPO 1999 (the firm's own listing), acq. by Conexant for $980M in 2000. ATM and packet-processing chipsets, funded 1996.

mammoth-media.note: Mobile-first media studio; the firm's own current field records the company as acquired. Site states a Series A entry.

managed-comp.note: Managed workers' compensation, funded 1996; last listed Private and its later course is not established on the record.

mandolin.note: AI automation for specialty drug access; site states a Series A entry.

manugistics-inc.note: IPO 1993 (the firm's own listing), acq. by JDA Software for $211M in 2006. Supply-chain planning, funded 1986.

mapinfo-corporation.note: IPO 1994 (the firm's own listing), acq. by Pitney Bowes for $408M in 2007. Desktop mapping and location data, funded 1989.

matrixx-software.note: Real-time charging and rating for telecom operators; still independent.

mazu-networks.note: Network behaviour analysis funded 2000; acq. by Riverbed Technology, 2009.

mccormack-and-dodge-corp.note: acq. by Dun & Bradstreet, 1983 (the firm's own listing). Mainframe financial applications, funded 1980; later part of Geac.

media-metrix.note: IPO 1999 (the firm's own listing); merged with Jupiter Communications in 2000 to form Jupiter Media Metrix, which is carried as the successor row. Internet audience measurement, funded 1997.

meditech.note: Medical Information Technology (MEDITECH), hospital information systems, funded 1986; still independent and privately held.

medium.note: Ev Williams' publishing platform; Greylock (David Sze) led an early round and the site states a Series A entry.

mentor-graphics-corporation.note: IPO 1984 (the firm's own listing), acq. by Siemens for $4.5B in 2017. Electronic design automation, funded 1981 — the oldest position the archive names with a year, and a pre-registered membership key row.

messageme.note: Mobile messaging funded 2013; the team was acquihired by Yahoo in 2014.

micom.note: IPO 1981, taken private by Odyssey Partners 1988 and acq. by Northern Telecom 1996 (the firm's own listing). Data multiplexers, funded 1979.

millennium-pharmaceuticals.note: IPO 1996 (the firm's own listing), acq. by Takeda for $8.8B in 2008. Gene-based therapeutics, funded 1993; the funds' 1997 13G is the filing evidence.

millipore.note: Separation and filtration equipment, funded 1969 — one of the firm's first positions. Long NYSE-listed and acq. by Merck KGaA for $7.2B in 2010.

mitotix.note: Cell-cycle therapeutics funded 1992; acq. by GPC Biotech, 2000.

mobile-automation.note: PC systems management funded 1997; acq. by iPass, 2004.

modular.note: Modular AI, Chris Lattner's Mojo and MAX AI platform; Greylock seeded it. The firm's own current field records the company as acquired, which postdates this judge's knowledge — published as the site has it and flagged for the A/B pass to name the acquirer.

molecular-design-ltd-inc.note: acq. by Maxwell Communication (Maxwell-Macmillan), 1987 (the firm's own listing); later MDL Information Systems under Elsevier. Chemical research databases, funded 1983.

molecular-dynamics-inc.note: IPO 1993 (the firm's own listing), acq. by Amersham Pharmacia Biotech, 1998. Life-science instrumentation, funded 1992.

multi.note: Multi (formerly Remotion), multiplayer screen sharing; acq. by Salesforce, 2024. Site states a Series A entry.

music-nation.note: Online music competition funded 2006; the site closed.

musical-ly.note: acq. by ByteDance for ~$800M-$1B in 2017 and merged into TikTok in 2018. Site states a Series A entry.

mutual-risk-management.note: IPO 1991 (the firm's own listing); the group collapsed in 2002 after reserve write-downs and went into run-off. Domiciled in Hamilton, BERMUDA — but run.py's ISO_OF table has no BM entry, so the country cannot be published truthfully and the row carries the firm's own region (US Eastern) with country_conflict rather than a null that would fail invariant 1. Adding BM to ISO_OF is requested at close; the same class as the seven missing countries added in bdd1534.

narrative-communications-inc.note: acq. by @Home Network, 1998 (the firm's own listing). Rich-media ad delivery, funded 1996.

natoma.note: Non-human identity governance; acq. by Okta, 2025. Greylock seeded it.

nauto.note: Fleet driver-behaviour AI; site states a Series B entry, which the gate clears.

neeva.note: Ad-free consumer search founded by Sridhar Ramaswamy, who joined Greylock afterwards; acq. by Snowflake, 2023. Site states a Series A entry.

net-effect-systems.note: acq. by Ask Jeeves, 1999 (the firm's own listing). Web customer support, funded 1998.

netic.note: AI revenue engine for essential service industries; a 2025 seed.

netnumina.note: NetNumina Solutions, financial-services systems integration funded 2000; last listed Private and its later course is not established.

netscout-inc.note: NetScout Systems (Nasdaq: NTCT); the firm's own listing still said Private, which the base overrides. Network monitoring, funded 1996. Market cap pinned in the A/B pass.

neurex.note: IPO 1993 (the firm's own listing), acq. by Elan for $700M in 1998. Cardiorenal and neurological therapeutics, funded 1987.

neutrogena.note: IPO 1973 (the firm's own listing), acq. by Johnson & Johnson for $924M in 1994. Dermatological skincare — the firm's earliest consumer position.

new-edge-networks.note: DSL competitive carrier funded 2000; acq. by EarthLink, 2006.

newview-technologies.note: Collaborative commerce for direct materials funded 1999; wound down after the B2B marketplace bust.

nocpulse.note: Infrastructure monitoring funded 2000; acq. by Red Hat, 2002, and became the basis of Red Hat Network Satellite.

northpoint-communications.note: IPO 1999 (the firm's own listing); the DSL carrier filed for bankruptcy in January 2001 after the Verizon merger collapsed and its assets went to AT&T.

notable.note: AI automation of physician-patient administrative work; Greylock seeded it.

novi.note: Product-data authority for AI-driven commerce; site states a Series A entry.

ntru-cryptosystems.note: Lattice-based cryptography funded 2000; acq. by Security Innovation, 2009, and the NTRU algorithms later fed the NIST post-quantum process. The same position as the ntru-inc row, merged at the rebuild.

ntru-inc.note: The same NTRU position under its second listed name; merged onto ntru-cryptosystems in identity-merges.json.

nuro.note: Autonomous delivery and the Nuro Driver licensing business; Greylock and Banyan led the 2017 Series A and the site states a Series A entry. Last priced at $6B in 2024 — pinned in the A/B pass.

oak.note: AI-native identity operating system; a 2023 seed.

oat-systems.note: RFID middleware funded 2003; acq. by Checkpoint Systems, 2008.

obsidian-security.note: SaaS security posture and threat detection; Greylock announced the investment in June 2017 and the site states a Series A entry.

octane-software-inc.note: CRM software funded 1998; acq. by E.piphany for $3.2B in stock, 2000.

okta.note: Greylock joined the $16.5M SERIES B of Aug 2011 with Khosla; a16z led the 2010 Series A. Golden-set row. IPO 2017 (Nasdaq: OKTA); market cap pinned in the A/B pass.

one-kings-lane.note: Flash-sale home decor funded 2011; acq. by Bed Bath & Beyond in 2016 and later sold on to CSC Generation.

onehouse.note: Managed Apache Hudi data lakehouse, from the creator of Hudi; Greylock seeded it.

ontogeny-inc.note: Developmental-biology therapeutics funded 1994 (Bill Helman); merged with Creative BioMolecules and Reprogenesis in 2000 to form Curis, which the firm's own 2013 card records as 'Merged with Creative BioMolecules in 2000'.
